title: Large semantic models in Power BI Premium

claims.text: Semantic models hold data in a highly compressed in-memory cache to deliver fast interactive query performance, and the default model size limit without the large storage format is 1 GB.

Enabling the large semantic model storage format raises the model size ceiling to the size of the Fabric capacity itself, or to a maximum set by the capacity administrator; it is available on Fabric F, Premium P, and Embedded A SKUs as well as Premium Per User.

The Power BI Desktop upload limit stays at 10 GB even with the large storage format; a model only grows past that ceiling inside the service through refresh, typically driven by an incremental refresh policy.

Turn on the large semantic model storage format whenever XMLA-based tools will perform write operations against the model, even if the model is small, because the large format improves XMLA write performance.

Behind the large-format toggle, the model's service storage mode changes from ABF (Analysis Services backup file) to Premium Files, which is why the feature is only offered in Azure regions that support Azure Premium Files storage.

Large-format models default to a VertiPaq segment size of 8 million rows, the same segment size used by Azure Analysis Services, chosen to balance memory consumption against query performance and to keep performance comparable when migrating models from Azure Analysis Services.

The service uses dynamic memory management to evict inactive semantic models from capacity memory, letting the combined size of all models far exceed the SKU's memory; a single model, however, is still bound by the SKU memory limit, and reloading an evicted model can add noticeable query delay.

On-demand load, enabled by default for large-format models, pages only the relevant data pages into memory rather than loading the whole model, which makes evicted models answer queries again much faster.

With on-demand load active, the DISCOVER_STORAGE_TABLE_COLUMN_SEGMENTS dynamic management view exposes per-column Temperature and Last Accessed statistics that reveal which columns are actually paged in and how the model is used.

A model's in-memory footprint can be estimated from VertiPaq storage DMVs by summing the DICTIONARY_SIZE values from DISCOVER_STORAGE_TABLE_COLUMNS with the USED_SIZE values from DISCOVER_STORAGE_TABLE_COLUMN_SEGMENTS, queried over the XMLA endpoint from SSMS.

Refreshing a model whose size approaches half the capacity's memory (for example a 12 GB model on a 25 GB capacity) risks running out of memory mid-refresh; mitigate by issuing fine-grained refreshes through the enhanced refresh REST API or the XMLA endpoint instead of full refreshes.
Once a large-format semantic model exists in a workspace, that workspace cannot be reassigned to a capacity in a different region, and push semantic models cannot use the large storage format at all.
